answer: Distinct Silicon Fingerprints. Each agent identity must run on hardware whose die-level timing variation is measured at enrollment and rechecked per epoch through a local challenge. An operator can buy many machines but cannot forge these per-chip variations, so each identity ties to one physical device and cloning is detectable. To scale, an attacker must acquire and maintain many independent devices; one sonnet of compute won't substitute. Enrollment hardware, spares, and revalidation effort set a real per-identity cost.
